supporting_observations.claim: During the alerted window, WS-MFISCHER-01 repeatedly connected to the internal proxy at approximately five-minute intervals: 13:41, 13:45, 13:50, 13:55, 14:00, 14:05, and 14:10 UTC.

Several of those proxy connections have similar byte counts, including roughly 4 KB sent and 13 KB received, which is consistent with recurring application traffic but does not identify the application or destination.

The cadence is plausibly consistent with the approved LedgerLink updater's stated five-minute update checks, but the available records do not link these connections to that updater or to update.ledgerlink.com.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records for the recurring activity are Zeek connection summaries to the internal proxy on port 8080; they do not show the HTTPS CONNECT destination, hostname, or proxy decision details.
The supplied recurring-connection records do not identify the originating process or executable on WS-MFISCHER-01.
claims_not_established: Whether the recurring connections were made by the approved LedgerLink updater or by another process.
Whether the connections reached update.ledgerlink.com or an unapproved destination.
Whether the traffic carried malicious content or data exfiltration.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy CONNECT or equivalent logs for the listed connection times, including requested hostnames, status, and byte counts.
Endpoint process-to-network telemetry or application logs correlating the connections to a process and user.
LedgerLink updater logs or configuration confirming whether it checked for updates during these times.
unrelated_findings: A connection from WS-MFISCHER-01 to 10.55.10.24 on PostgreSQL port 5432 appears in the evidence; review separately because it is outside the alerted periodic proxy activity.

DC-SUN-01 initiated connections toward WS-MFISCHER-01 on ports 80, 135, 8080, and 443 around 13:59 UTC; some attempts were rejected or reset. Review separately and do not use these attempts to decide the alerted activity.
